text: A community needs a new public library on a difficult site. Which part of the architecture work would you most want to own?

options.text: Turn the community's needs into a clear brief, room plan, and circulation layout.
Shape the building's form, daylight, materials, and relationship to the street.
Calculate the structural system and coordinate technical building services.
Study how the library could support learning, access, and neighborhood activity.

text: Which studio assignment would keep you engaged through a long architecture course?

options.text: Design a small home for a family, balancing privacy, comfort, cost, and climate.
Rework a crowded street so walking, public transport, and local shops work better together.
Create a low-energy building using passive cooling, shade, and locally suitable materials.
Develop a precise digital model and drawings that help a team coordinate construction.

text: A design looks striking but exceeds the client's budget. What would you most enjoy doing next?

options.text: Revise the design creatively while keeping its main experience and purpose.
Compare materials and construction methods to find practical savings.
Talk with the client to rank needs and agree what can change.
Test the design against accessibility, safety, and local building requirements.

text: What would you most like to notice and understand when you enter an unfamiliar building?

options.text: How people move through it and whether the spaces feel intuitive.
How its structure carries loads and how it was assembled.
How light, sound, texture, and proportion affect the atmosphere.
How the building uses energy and responds to its climate and surroundings.

text: Two people give conflicting accounts of an agreement. Which part of resolving the dispute would interest you most?

options.text: Read the contract closely and identify what each clause requires.
Question each account, test the evidence, and prepare arguments for a hearing.
Help both sides negotiate a workable settlement before a lengthy case.
Research the relevant law and explain the likely outcomes clearly to a client.

text: Which legal issue would you most want to study in depth?

options.text: Business contracts, company decisions, and mergers.
Criminal justice, fair trials, and the rights of accused people.
Privacy, online harm, and the rules that should govern new technology.
Patents, trademarks, and protecting creative or scientific work.

text: Which typical law task sounds most satisfying to you?

options.text: Present a clear argument in court and respond to questions from a judge.
Draft and review agreements so a business can make a decision safely.
Research cases and legislation, then write a careful legal opinion.
Explain legal choices to a person or organization and help them decide what to do.

text: A local community may be affected by a new policy. What would you most want to contribute as a legal professional?

options.text: Make sure people understand their rights and can access legal help.
Check whether the policy follows constitutional and statutory requirements.
Advise organizations on how to comply and reduce legal risks.
Research the policy's effects and recommend fairer legal protections.

text: A company is negotiating a major partnership. Which legal task would you most want to take on?

options.text: Review the commercial terms and identify risks in the agreement.
Research whether the proposed arrangement meets company and competition rules.
Negotiate language that protects both sides while keeping the deal workable.
Assess how customer data and intellectual property will be protected.

text: Which question at the intersection of law and business would you most enjoy exploring?

options.text: How should companies be governed and held accountable?
How should a business protect a new product, brand, or invention?
How should online businesses use personal data responsibly?
How should disputes between businesses be resolved fairly and efficiently?

text: Which responsibility would you prefer in a legal team supporting a growing company?

options.text: Drafting contracts and advising teams before they enter business deals.
Researching laws and writing guidance that explains practical choices.
Investigating a dispute and preparing evidence for negotiation or court.
Building a compliance process that helps the company meet its obligations.

text: A new regulation changes how a business can operate. Which response sounds most interesting to you?

options.text: Interpret the rules and explain what the company must change.
Assess whether the regulation protects people while treating businesses fairly.
Help design internal training and checks so teams follow the rules.
Research how the change affects contracts, customers, and future strategy.

text: A new technology raises questions about privacy and ownership. Which legal work would interest you most?

options.text: Research how privacy laws apply to the technology and its users.
Help protect the invention through patents and intellectual property rights.
Advise the company on contracts, licensing, and commercial risk.
Explain the legal issue clearly to affected people and help them understand their options.

text: Which task sounds most rewarding in a career that combines careful reading, reasoning, and communication?

options.text: Build a persuasive case from facts, evidence, and legal precedents.
Write a precise agreement that makes responsibilities clear.
Compare different interpretations of a law and explain the strongest one.
Help two sides reach a fair agreement through negotiation.

text: A health company launches a new product. Which legal question would you most want to investigate?

options.text: Whether the product claims are supported and meet health regulations.
How patient information should be protected when the product uses digital records.
Who owns the research, formula, or brand behind the product.
How to explain a person's rights and options after a product-related complaint.

text: Which kind of work would you prefer in a legal career connected to healthcare and science?

options.text: Research laws and policies that affect patients and public health.
Review company agreements and help organizations follow regulations.
Protect medical inventions, research discoveries, and trademarks.
Help people understand a dispute and prepare a clear argument for resolution.

text: A patient is prescribed several medicines and is worried about side effects. Which part of helping them would you most want to do?

options.text: Check the medicines for interactions and explain safe use in clear language.
Study how the medicines work in the body and why the side effects occur.
Test medicine samples and verify their quality in a laboratory.
Help develop and evaluate a safer formulation for future patients.

text: Which pharmaceutical science project would you choose for a semester?

options.text: Compare dosage forms and find a way to make a medicine easier to take.
Analyze how a drug is absorbed, distributed, and cleared from the body.
Inspect a production process and identify where quality checks are needed.
Review evidence about whether a treatment is safe and effective for patients.

text: A medicine batch fails a quality check. What would you be most interested in investigating?

options.text: Trace the production steps to find what caused the variation.
Run further tests to confirm the product's strength, purity, and stability.
Check the records and standards that govern the release of the batch.
Assess whether the issue could affect patients already using the medicine.

text: Which work setting in the medicines field sounds most appealing for your future?

options.text: A hospital or community pharmacy, helping people use medicines safely.
A pharmaceutical company developing and manufacturing medicines.
A quality or regulatory team checking that medicines meet required standards.
A research lab studying drug action, formulation, or delivery.
